svg.text: Day 20 - speculative-decoding draft-tree verifier (multi-GPU / heterogeneous inference)
draft tree in on-chip flops · all N children tested in parallel · log-depth argmax picks the winner in the same cycle · one accepted token per clock
APB3 control PSEL PENABLE PWRITE PADDR[11:0] PWDATA[31:0]
CTRL · TH_ABS · TH_REL · MAX_ACC · STATUS · IRQ_STAT (W1C) · ERRCODE · CAPS · 10 counters · HIST[0..MAX_DEPTH-1]
emits one node record per proposed token:
{parent, draft tok, target argmax, score, pmax}
AXI4-Stream ingress S_TVALID / S_TREADY S_TDATA[127:0] S_TLAST (end of tree)
w0[15:0] parent (0xFFFF = root) · w1 draft token · w2 target argmax at this position
w3[15:0] score = P(this token) Q0.16 · w3[31:16] pmax = best P at this position

g.text: HIST[k]: tokens accepted at depth k

svg.text: 64 x 112 flops - the whole tree on chip

g.text: node 0 par 0xFFFF | tok | pred | score | thr
node 1 par | tok | pred | score | thr
node 2 par | tok | pred | score | thr
node 63 par | tok | pred | score | thr

svg.text: keeps the multiplier out of the walk's critical path
64 parent + 64 token + 64 score compares, one cycle
a malformed tree costs one cycle, not a half-walk
merge rule: take the right child only if it is
valid AND strictly greater - so ties fall to the
lower index structurally, not by comparison
this replaces the CPU's inner sweep

g.text: CHECK 1 cycle, whole tree, and waits
for the FIFO to drain first
cur <= argmax idx; push on k+1

svg.text: only the load term depends on the tree size
holds a whole job: MAX_DEPTH tokens
+ 1 trailer, so the walk never stalls on
one beat per clock when ready.
TLAST travels with the data, so the
reader frames a job as it arrives
EN, MAX_ACC, SOFT_RST (latched on the first beat of a job)
job_done / node_inc / accept_inc + depth / err / clamp / stall strobes
AXI4-Stream egress M_TVALID / M_TREADY M_TDATA[127:0] M_TLAST (trailer)
accepted-token beat: w0 node index · w1 token · w2 score · w3 depth
trailer beat: w0 accepted count · w1 bonus token · w2 error code · w3 (nodes << 16) | CLAMP
the node indices are what tell the runtime which KV-cache rows to keep
host consumes the beats: accepted tokens, bonus token, KV rows to keep
